Supervise local corrections with a projection-aware energy oracle.
Training geometry only; no optimized target trajectory labels.

The analytic energy measures footprint clearance, goal progress, retreat, early heading, and smoothness. The oracle normalizes and caps the gradient, then selects a step that remains acceptable after projection. The label is a local direction, not an optimized target trajectory.

During training, geometric energy measures goal-directed progress, clearance around the robot footprint, and motion regularity. Its local descent direction provides supervision.

Oracle targets are aggregated across model-visited candidate paths.

We initialize candidate paths, query correction labels, retain them in replay, and train GEAR on the accumulated states. The learned model advances the path frontier. The full-dataset continuation uses the current model to generate states and learns from oracle labels on those states.

The energy oracle supplies a projection-aware correction at the current candidate path. GEAR learns to predict this correction from the image, goal, and path.

Train on paths the model visits

The model determines the paths it will encounter next. We query the energy oracle at those model-visited paths and retain labels from prior rounds. An energy acceptance guard is used during training collection only.

Each model update changes the next candidate path. We query new correction labels at these visited paths and retain earlier rounds in a shared replay dataset.

GEAR model: learn a correction field

The pretrained visual-language model provides context, while the waypoint expert sees the current trajectory. GEAR predicts a correction and applies a bounded update. This loop is reused at deployment without an ESDF, energy gradient, or energy acceptance test.

Current GEAR-Nav manuscript and its figure PDFs. Original native DRIVE clips retain their exact source IDs, intervals, mute and autoplay settings. All clips play at 1×. Comparisons are representative separate trials. No quantitative performance claim is added.
Figure source: GEAR-Nav Overleaf/fig/gear_model_simple.pdf, architecture panel (a). Action-free describes navigation adaptation; the pretrained backbone may have robot-action pretraining.
At deployment, visual and goal context condition the waypoint expert. It predicts a correction, applies a bounded path update, and repeats. No ESDF or energy query is required.
00:45–00:55. Reveal inputs, model, bounded update, then the feedback arrow. Keep training-only geometry absent. The backbone is pretrained; the recorded example uses adapter-only training.
